deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics: no formulas, derivations or computations. It belongs to the methodological introduction of Riemann's unfinished 'Mechanik des Ohres', published posthumously by Henle in 1867 (Zeitschrift für rationelle Medicin, 3. Reihe, Bd. 29) and reprinted in the Gesammelte Werke. The marginal 'p. 5' and the next page's 'p. 6' place it in the draft sequence.

(a) Top line, continuing the previous page: following the same principles, the 'Leistungen' (performances) of the hearing organ must first be carefully established for our purpose. This sentence is redrafted at the top of p. 6.

(b) Section III, boxed paragraph on testing the explanation against experience. An explanation of the organ can be checked in two ways:
  (i) through its consequences for the organ's performances;
  (ii) through the physical properties of the organ's components that the explanation presupposes.
For (i), exact comparison with experience is extremely difficult. One must often restrict oneself to the question whether any result of perception or observation contradicts the theory. For (ii), the inferred physical properties can be of more general interest and can advance knowledge of the laws of nature. Riemann's example is Helmholtz's attempt to explain the accommodation of the eye (Handbuch der physiologischen Optik, 1856-67; the 1855 accommodation paper). This passage corresponds closely to the printed text.

(c) Lower half, written upside down and largely struck through. It is an earlier outline of the same introduction, with numbered points:
  1) Der Gegenstand ...
  2) Die Wahrnehmung/Untersuchung ...
  3) ... und die Prüfung an der Erfahrung ...
It also contains phrases about the use of analogies, the organ and the theory, echoing the previous page's warning about 'die nachtheiligen Folgen der Benutzung von Analogien'.

In modern terms the content is a philosophy-of-science statement about inverse ('synthetic') explanation of an organ from its function. It distinguishes necessary assumptions (forced by established natural laws) from arbitrary modelling choices, and favours falsification-style testing.
errors: No mathematical errors possible: the page contains no mathematics. The text is a heavily corrected draft; the wording is unsettled (e.g. 'müssen ... festgestellt werden' mixes constructions, later revised on p. 6).

results.what: Two-way scheme for testing a physiological-mechanical explanation: via predicted performances of the organ and via presupposed physical properties of its parts. Exact comparison is often replaced by checking that no observation contradicts the theory. Example: Helmholtz's theory of accommodation of the eye.
results.modern_name: Methodology of model validation / hypothetico-deductive testing (falsification criterion avant la lettre)
results.usually_credited_to: General 19th-century methodology (Newton/Herbart terminology cited by Riemann); falsification as a doctrine to Popper (1934)

deep.surprise_reason: This is the known draft of the introduction to Riemann's 'Mechanik des Ohres', published in 1867 and in the Werke; its methodological remarks are well known and discussed. The page contains no mathematics.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 reads more like 'Nach denselben Principien müssten wir für unseren Zweck zunächst die Leistungen des Gehörorgans sorgfältig festgestellt werden' (struck word after 'müssten'). Compare the redraft at the top of p. 6.
Left margin beside Section III: 'p. 5.' (page number of the draft).
'theils die Folgerungen dienen' – likely 'theils die Folgerungen [dienen], die sich aus ihr für die Leistungen des Organs ergeben'. The struck word before 'Organs' appears to be an aborted 'Gehör-'.

'und man muss [-…-] häufig der Theorie nach {+die Frage+} … auf beschränken' is best read as 'und man muss sich häufig ... auf die Frage beschränken, ob kein Ergebniss einer Wahrnehmung oder einer Beobachtung ihr widerspricht' (cf. the printed text).

The interlinear insertion 'Folgerungen über die physikalischen Eigenschaften der Bestandtheile' replaces the struck 'physikalischen Eigenschaften'. The sentence reads: 'Was dagegen die Folgerungen über die physikalischen Eigenschaften der Bestandtheile betrifft, so können diese von allgemeinerem Interesse sein ...'
'Erkenntniss der Naturgesetze' follows a struck 'Physik'; 'Accommodation des Auges durch Helmholtz der Fall war' is correctly read.

The upside-down lower half is an earlier draft outline of the introduction (items 1)–3) plus a struck paragraph on analogies and the testing of theory). It is not new content; most words are unrecoverable, and the machine fragments should be treated as uncertain.
